info.title: Loud Radish — Live Audio & Video Transcriber
info.summary: Live seminar transcription with an LLM assistant over the running transcript.

get.description: Report that the process is alive, and which optional capabilities are installed.
The current session and pipeline state.

post.description: Begin capture and transcription in the requested capture mode.

Start if idle, stop if running (D-023's companion, and Plan 5's whole control surface).

**One endpoint rather than two** because a keystroke has no way to know the current state, and
a round trip to find out is a race: press the key twice quickly and the second request reads a
state the first has already changed. Deciding it server-side, where the lock is, removes the
race rather than narrowing it.
End the session and return its final statistics.

get.description:
Microphones and loopback devices in one merged list, each tagged with its type.

Unavailability is reported rather than hidden: an empty list with no explanation looks like a
broken feature, whereas one naming the install command is actionable.

post.description:
Open a capture device briefly and report whether it is actually producing usable audio.

Enumerating a device proves only that the host knows about it. Whether the microphone is
plugged into the socket the driver means, unmuted, and at a workable gain is a different
question, and every one of those failures looks identical until the talk has started and the
transcript is empty. No audio is retained (BE §17).

schema.title: Response Test Device Api Audio Test Post

get.description:
Recordings the file source can replay.

``audio.file_path`` is a path on this machine, and a browser can neither browse that filesystem
nor resolve one from a file picker. Without this list the only way to choose a recording is to
edit the config file by hand — which is the kind of step this application exists not to need.

schema.title: Response Get Audio Files Api Audio Files Get

post.description:
Add a recording to the library and select it.

Selecting it immediately is the point: uploading a file and then having to pick it from a list
is two steps to express one intention.

schema.title: Response Upload Audio File Api Audio Files Post

delete.description: Remove a recording from the library. Refuses anything outside it.

schema.title: Response Delete Audio File Api Audio Files Delete

post.description: Choose the capture source. Takes effect when the next session starts.

schema.title: Response Select Device Api Audio Device Post

get.description: Every backend with the information needed to choose between them (FE §7.2).

post.description: Load a model. Progress arrives over the WebSocket as ``asr.progress``.

schema.title: Response Load Model Api Asr Load Post

post.description: Free the model and its device memory — relevant when a local LLM shares the GPU.

schema.title: Response Unload Model Api Asr Unload Post

post.description: Set the biasing prompt. Live: it applies to the next inference pass.

schema.title: Response Set Session Prompt Api Asr Prompt Post

get.description:
Which transcription passes this session holds (D-022).

Usually one. A window session that ran both a live pass and a post-capture one holds two, and
the transcript pane offers a Live/Final switch only when it does — a switch between one thing
and itself is chrome that explains nothing.

schema.title: Response Revisions Api Transcript Revisions Get

get.description: Every segment from one pass. What the Live/Final switch fetches.
Everything after ``segment_id``. Ordered by id, which makes the replay idempotent.
Everything overlapping a time range — what "summarise the last ten minutes" reads.
Full-text search. A query that FTS5 cannot parse returns nothing rather than an error.
The running outline of the talk.

The transcript rewritten for reading, oldest block first.

Read on every page load, and empty on a machine with no language model — which is why it uses
the optional store: "nothing has been polished" is the ordinary state, not a failure.
The session glossary, in order of first appearance.
Download the transcript in one of the five formats.
The full resolved configuration.

patch.description:
Apply dotted-path changes and report what applying them costs.

The hot-swap class comes back with the response so the frontend can warn *before* the user
commits to something that will interrupt transcription (BE §13.3).

post.description: Apply a named profile — Accuracy, Balanced, or Low resource.
Persist runtime changes to the user config file. Credentials are never written.

schema.title: Response Save Config Api Config Save Post

get.description: Both provider configurations, and whether a credential exists. Never a credential value.

put.description:
Store a credential in the OS credential store.

A failure here is reported rather than swallowed: a key the user believes is saved but is not
produces an authentication failure much later, with nothing connecting it to this moment.

schema.title: Response Put Credential Api Llm Credential Put

delete.description: Remove a stored credential. Removing one that was never there is not an error.

schema.title: Response Delete Credential Api Llm Credential  Provider  Delete

get.description:
Models the configured endpoint reports.

A failure is a 200 with an empty list and an explanation, not an HTTP error: this is called to
populate a dropdown while the user is still typing an address, and a red error for "you have
not finished typing the URL yet" is noise.

schema.title: Response Get Llm Models Api Llm Models Get

post.description:
Probe the provider and report one of four specific outcomes.

Accepts an optional partial LLM configuration so the settings form can test what is on screen
rather than what is saved.

get.description:
A cheap description of the assistant's readiness, with no network call.

The header reads this to decide between "Assistant ready" and "Assistant not set up", and it is
read on every page load — so it must never wait on a model server that may not be running.

schema.title: Response Get Llm Status Api Llm Status Get

post.description: Ask a question. The answer streams over the WebSocket.
Stop the in-flight answer. Cancelling nothing is not an error.

schema.title: Response Cancel Api Chat Cancel Post

get.description: The conversation so far.

delete.description: Clear the conversation. The transcript is untouched.

schema.title: Response Clear History Api Chat History Delete

get.description: The configured one-tap prompts.

post.description:
Record how far the user has read, so "what did I miss" has a starting point.

Held on the server rather than in the browser so it survives a reload — losing it mid-talk
turns the action into "summarise everything", which is a different and much less useful thing.

schema.title: Response Mark Read Api Chat Read Post

get.description:
Every session on disk, newest first.

Includes files that cannot be read, each with its reason. A session the user can see and cannot
open is more useful than one that has silently vanished from the list.

schema.title: Response List Sessions Api Sessions Get

get.description: One past session's transcript, summaries, and glossary.

schema.title: Response Read Session Api Sessions  Key  Get

delete.description:
Delete a past session file.

Refuses the session that is currently recording: deleting the file out from under an open
connection loses the talk in progress, which is the one thing this application must not do.

schema.title: Response Delete Session Api Sessions  Key  Delete

get.description:
Download a past session in any of the five formats.

**The conversation is not in it unless it is asked for.** Markdown and JSON used to carry the
questions the user put to the assistant during the recording, because they were the two formats
that could. But a transcript export is mostly a thing being handed to somebody else, and one
person's half of a conversation is not part of the record of the talk. It exports on its own
from ``/{key}/chat``; `include_chat=true` puts it back in here for anyone who wants one file.

Download the conversation the user had with the assistant during this recording.

Its own document, because it belongs to the person who asked rather than to the talk. Empty is
a valid answer and renders as a sentence saying so, rather than a 404 — "you asked nothing
during this recording" is information, and an error code is not.

The recording itself, for the export window's preview player.

**Served with range support**, which `FileResponse` provides: a `<video>` element seeking a
hundreds-of-megabytes file over a route that could only send the whole thing would download all
of it to show a frame two minutes in.

The path is resolved from the key rather than taken from the request — the same rule every
route here follows, because a loopback-bound server is still reachable from any page in any
browser, and a route that served a path would serve any file on the machine.

What this recording is, and what each preset would turn it into (D-037).

**The measurement is the point.** A preset list on its own says "720p"; this says what 720p
means for *this* file — the reported seminar asked for a 720p ceiling at capture and recorded
at 2560 x 1532, so a window offering choices against the configured number would be describing
a recording that does not exist.

Every size is a range and says so. A constant-quality encode depends on content the estimator
has not watched, and a figure presented as exact would be wrong in the way that matters, since
the whole question is whether a file is small enough to send.

schema.title: Response Export Options Api Sessions  Key  Export Options Get

post.description:
Begin an export, and return the job to watch it by.

A request, not a download. An encode is minutes for an hour of talk, and the old synchronous
route held a browser connection open for the whole of it — tolerable for a stream copy and not
for this. Progress arrives over the WebSocket; `export/result` collects the file.

schema.title: Response Start Export Api Sessions  Key  Export Start Post

get.description:
The current or most recent export for this session.

The reconciliation path, exactly as `GET /api/session` is for the live pipeline: the WebSocket
is how progress arrives and this is how a page that has just loaded finds out where things got
to without waiting for the next frame.

schema.title: Response Export Status Api Sessions  Key  Export Status Get

post.description: Stop an export that is running. The partial output is removed rather than left playable.

schema.title: Response Cancel Export Api Sessions  Key  Export Cancel Post

get.description:
Download what the export produced.

Separate from the request that started it, so a finished export survives a reload — the archive
is on disk in the recording's own folder, and this is the route that hands it over.

Download this recording as a self-contained HTML web application, in a ZIP.

Refused rather than degraded when the recording has no video or no transcript. A "web
application" with an empty player and nothing to read is not the thing that was asked for, and
shipping one under the same name disappoints quietly instead of explaining — so the refusal
names which piece is missing and what to do about it.

Built on a worker thread. A talk is hundreds of megabytes, and copying that much into an archive
on the event loop stalls every other request including the transcript the user is watching.

**The archive carries the talk and not the conversation about it**, unless `include_chat` says
otherwise. The exported page's whole purpose is that whoever receives it connects their own
model and asks their own questions; opening it to find the panel already half-full of someone
else's questions, about a talk they have not watched, is the opposite of that.

Every recording still on disk, newest first.

A recording present here has *not* been transcribed, or was kept deliberately: the pass deletes
its audio on success unless audio retention is on. So this list is mostly a list of things that
went wrong, which is exactly what it is for.

Addressed by folder key — ``20260829-174113-d60b37a9e3c4`` — rather than by file name, since a
recording is now a directory holding audio, video, a preview frame, and a sidecar.

schema.title: Response List Recordings Api Recordings Get

post.description:
Run — or re-run — a transcription pass over a recording on disk.

Writes into a **new** session rather than the one that produced the recording. The original
session's database may hold a partial transcript from a pass that failed halfway, and appending
a second attempt to it would interleave two runs into one unreadable record.

schema.title: Response Transcribe Recording Api Recordings  Name  Transcribe Post

delete.description: Remove a recording. Refuses one a transcription pass is currently reading.

schema.title: Response Delete Recording Api Recordings  Name  Delete

get.description: What the monitor pane draws. Reports `recording: false` when nothing is capturing.

schema.title: Response Capture State Api Capture State Get

get.description:
The most recent preview frame.

404 whenever there is not one — no capture, no `jpegenc`, or the first frame not yet written.
The monitor treats that as its documented degraded state and shows a static card, because a
black rectangle and a broken preview look identical (D-020).
The live application: transcript pane, chat pane, header, status bar.
Past sessions, with export. Everything it shows arrives over ``/api/sessions``.

AsrModelsResponse.title: AsrModelsResponse
AsrModelsResponse.description: Every backend, including ones that cannot run here, with the reason attached.

CaptureOptions.title: CaptureOptions
CaptureOptions.description:
Per-run switches collected before capture begins (D-020).

Deliberately per-run rather than configuration: a user who recorded one window without video
should not silently get no video the next time. Only ``window`` mode reads them; the other two
have nothing to choose.

All three false records nothing and is refused. The interface refuses it as a courtesy — this
is the rule.

ChatSendRequest.title: ChatSendRequest
ChatSendRequest.description: Ask a question. The answer streams over the WebSocket.

ChatSendResponse.title: ChatSendResponse
ChatSendResponse.description: Acknowledgement. The answer itself arrives as ``chat.delta`` frames.

ConfigPatchResponse.title: ConfigPatchResponse
ConfigPatchResponse.description: What applying the change costs the running session (BE §13.3).

ConfigResponse.title: ConfigResponse
ConfigResponse.description: The full resolved configuration, plus what each area costs to change.

ConnectionTestResponse.title: ConnectionTestResponse
ConnectionTestResponse.description: A specific result, never generic failure text (FE §7.3).

DeviceListResponse.title: DeviceListResponse
DeviceListResponse.description: Microphones and loopback devices in one merged list, each tagged with its type.

LlmConfigResponse.title: LlmConfigResponse
LlmConfigResponse.description:
Both provider configurations, and whether a credential exists.

**Never carries a credential value.** The frontend learns only whether one is present.

LlmCredentialRequest.title: LlmCredentialRequest
LlmCredentialRequest.description: Store a credential in the OS credential store.

PolishedBlocksResponse.title: PolishedBlocksResponse
PolishedBlocksResponse.description:
The transcript rewritten for reading, one block per finished minute (D-018).

Empty whenever no language model has been available — which is the ordinary state, and the
signal to the frontend that it should keep showing raw segments.

SessionPromptRequest.title: SessionPromptRequest
SessionPromptRequest.description: The biasing prompt the user pastes before the talk (BE §6.5).

SessionResponse.title: SessionResponse
SessionResponse.description: The current session and pipeline state.

SessionStoppedResponse.title: SessionStoppedResponse
SessionStoppedResponse.description: Final statistics for a session that has just ended.

StartSessionRequest.title: StartSessionRequest
StartSessionRequest.description: Optional metadata for a new session. Everything else comes from configuration.
